# Locating the OM651 Engine Serial Number on a Mercedes-Benz C220 CDI W204

Identifying the specific engine serial number (often referred to as the Engine Code or Motor Number) is a critical step in verifying the provenance of a powertrain unit, particularly when assessing whether an installation on a 2012 Mercedes-Benz C-Class C220 CDI (W204 chassis) is original. Unlike vehicle identification numbers (VINs), which are stamped into the chassis rail or dashboard pillar and serve to identify the entire car, engine serial numbers are specific to the block itself. For the OM651 3.0-liter V6 diesel found in this generation W204, locating this identifier requires a precise physical inspection rather than a simple lookup in the vehicle's documentation.

The primary location for the OM651 serial number is cast directly into the engine block. Specifically, you will find it on the passenger side (right-hand side) of the cylinder block, near the oil pan or lower transmission bell housing area. This marking is typically recessed into the casting and requires a flashlight and close inspection to read clearly. In many cases, the characters are not raised; they are stamped or etched below the surface level of the metal. To ensure you can read the full string of alphanumeric charactersâwhich usually includes a prefix indicating the plant code, a sequence number, and the date of manufactureâyou may need to clean the area with a rag and use a small magnifying tool if visibility is poor due to grime or oil accumulation.

It is crucial to distinguish between the VIN and the engine serial number during this inspection. The 17-digit VIN is located on the dashboard near the windshield, visible through the glass from the outside of the vehicle. While the VIN provides the complete history of the car, it does not replace the need for the engine code when verifying if a specific block was originally installed by the manufacturer. If you are evaluating a used unit or an engine swap, the factory will have recorded the serial number of the engine at the time of build against that specific VIN.

To verify originality, you must cross-reference the physical serial number found on the block with the data available in the vehicle's service history or the official Mercedes-Benz parts database. If you have access to a Vehicle Identification Number (VIN) decoder tool or a dealer portal, entering the 17-digit VIN should return the factory-installed engine code. A mismatch between the physical casting and the factory record indicates either an engine swap performed after purchase or a modification that warrants further investigation into the vehicle's maintenance history.

While digital solutions offer convenience for modern diagnostics, physical verification remains the gold standard for this specific inquiry. There are no software commands or API endpoints that will magically reveal the engine serial number without first locating the physical casting; the data is hardware-embedded. However, once located, you can utilize tools like OBD-II scanners that support reading engine calibration files to confirm if the Electronic Control Unit (ECU) matches the block's specifications, though this is a secondary verification step.
